content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Define what a deficiency disease is
Describe the causes and symptoms of common deficiency diseases
Explain how deficiency diseases can be prevented and treated
Understand the global importance of nutritional deficiencies

occur when the diet lacks essential nutrients. These diseases were common historically and remain significant health problems in many parts of the world. Understanding deficiency diseases helps explain the importance of a balanced diet containing all necessary nutrients.
A disease caused by lack of an essential nutrient in the diet.
Citrus fruits, berries, peppers, broccoli, tomatoes
Eat oily fish, eggs, fortified foods
Less haemoglobin = less oxygen to tissues
Eat iron-rich foods: red meat, leafy greens, beans
Rickets (in children, with vitamin D deficiency)
Swollen belly (oedema from low plasma proteins)
General wasting, not just protein shortage
In pregnancy: can cause cretinism in baby
Leading cause of preventable blindness in children
Deficiency diseases are still common because:
Deficiency diseases only occur in developing countries
Can occur anywhere with poor diet (e.g., elderly, fad diets)
Taking supplements is as good as eating well
Whole foods provide nutrients in optimal forms and combinations
If you're not thin, you can't have deficiencies
Overweight people can lack specific nutrients
Anaemia is always caused by low iron
Other deficiencies (B12, folate) can also cause anaemia
Disease caused by lack of nutrient
Poor vision in dim light from vitamin A deficiency
Deficiency diseases result from lack of essential nutrients
Scurvy (vitamin C): bleeding gums, poor wound healing
Rickets (vitamin D): soft bones, bowed legs
Still major global health problems, especially in developing countries
